articles.title: Shingletown Star Party
articles.summary: The Shingletown Star Party, a popular annual event for amateur astronomers, is set for its 4th year from Wednesday, July 6th, through Monday, July 11th. Located at Shingletown Airport near Mt. Lassen in Northern California, the event promises dark skies and a variety of daytime activities. Registration is now open, and further details, including a downloadable flyer for the 2005 event, are available on its official website.

articles.title: The Stars of Orion
articles.summary: This article provides an in-depth look at the major stars within the Orion constellation, offering details on their distances, characteristics, and eventual fates. It covers stars like Saiph, Betelgeuse, Bellatrix, Rigel, and the belt stars (Alnitak, Alnilam, Mintaka), along with a description of the Great Orion Nebula (M42/M43). The piece serves as a guide for viewing Orion during its final months of visibility.

articles.title: Mooning
articles.summary: This month's 'Moon column' is absent because author Dave North lacked inspiration for an April Fool's piece and was busy with observing activities during good weather. He briefly mentions upcoming celestial events, including a mostly-unobservable hybrid solar eclipse and an unexciting penumbral lunar eclipse on April 24th, which he notes will only make the Moon appear slightly dim. The author attributes the brevity of the column to a busy schedule of 'Actual Observing' and other outdoor pursuits.

articles.title: Auction XXV
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) is holding its annual astronomical auction and swap meet, "Auction XXV," on Sunday, April 24, 2005, at Houge Park in San Jose. This event provides an opportunity for beginners to acquire telescopes and for experienced observers to find various astronomical equipment, with an auction starting at 1 PM followed by a swap meet around 3 PM. Sellers pay a 10% commission, supporting the SJAA's educational endeavors.

articles.title: Board of Directors Elected
articles.summary: The article reports on the annual election of the Board of Directors, where four members were re-elected and Gordon Reade was newly elected. It also announces the death of Richard Barrett, a Mercury-News columnist whose 1954 column led to the founding of the San Jose Amateur Astronomers, now known as the San Jose Astronomical Association.

articles.title: Excellent SF Bay AreaGraze April 15 of Upsilon Geminorum
articles.summary: An excellent grazing occultation of the magnitude 4.1 star Upsilon Geminorum was predicted for the SF Bay Area on the evening of Friday, April 15, 2005. The event was highlighted as suitable for beginners due to the bright star, high lunar elevation, and convenient timing, with an expedition planned for south Fremont. The article detailed observation techniques, the predicted lunar profile, and several alternate viewing locations.

articles.title: New Theory about the Barringer Meteor Crater
articles.summary: Scientists have developed a new theory about the Barringer Meteor Crater, proposing that the meteor struck Earth at a much slower speed (around 12 km/sec) than previously thought and fragmented into a swarm of material during atmospheric entry. This revised model, based on sophisticated simulations by H. Jay Melosh and Gareth Collins, resolves the long-standing mystery of why there is not more impact-melted rock at the crater. The article also briefly touches on the timeline of human presence in North America relative to the impact event.

articles.title: Silicon Valley Astronomy Lecture Series
articles.summary: This article announces a free public lecture by Dr. Frank Drake, a pioneer in SETI, on April 20, 2005, discussing updated estimates for extraterrestrial life, incorporating recent exoplanet discoveries. It also provides comprehensive solar system statistics including Right Ascension, Declination, Distance, Magnitude, and Size for various celestial bodies throughout April 2005, adapted from observer handbooks.

articles.title: SJAA loaner scope status
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) provides an update on the status of its telescope loaner program, detailing which scopes are available for immediate borrowing, those currently on loan, and those with extended loan periods. Members can contact Mike Koop to borrow an available scope or be placed on a waiting list for popular models. The article also lists specific telescope types and the members currently storing or borrowing them.
